newsitem.title: HONG KONG: British envoy denies Britain softened on assembly.
newsitem.headline: British envoy denies Britain softened on assembly.

text.p: Britain's chief diplomat in Hong Kong said on Thursday London had not softened its posture towards the unelected legislature that China plans for the territory after it takes over next week.

Trade Commissioner Francis Cornish, soon to become Consul-General, said Britain hoped the Provisional Legislature would have a short lifespan and his decision to attend its swearing-in ceremony was not an endorsement of the body.
Cornish was responding to reports that Britain had done a U-turn on the appointed, pro-Beijing Provisional Legislature which will replace the territory's elected chamber on July 1.
"Nothing will persuade the British government that the dismissal of the Legislative Council is anything other than a step in the wrong direction," Cornish told reporters.
A planned British boycott of the body's swearing-in ceremony crumbled this week as the United States and then Britain itself decided to send senior envoys including Cornish to the event.
Analysts have widely interpreted these moves as a climbdown from the two countries' once tough opposition to the interim lawmaking assembly.
"It means no weakening of our attitude or position towards the Provisional Legislature which we hope and expect will be replaced as soon as possible with an election," Cornish said.
He said Britain wanted to see "a properly constituted Legislative Council" in conformity with the territory's future constitution promulgated by China, the Basic Law.
Cornish said he would attend the event because future leader Tung Chee-hwa would also be sworn in at the same time, as would his principal government officers and the judiciary.
"These are individuals and institutions which we support and which we want to work very closely with," Cornish said.
